Okay, so I need to find the sum of all prime numbers less than 200. Hmm, primes are numbers greater than 1 that have no positive divisors other than 1 and themselves. So, I guess I need to list all the prime numbers below 200 and then add them up. 

First, I should figure out a systematic way to list all primes less than 200. I remember something called the Sieve of Eratosthenes, which is an ancient algorithm for finding all primes up to any given limit. Maybe I can use that. Let me recall how it works. 

The Sieve of Eratosthenes works by iteratively marking the multiples of each prime number starting from 2. The numbers which remain unmarked at the end of the process are primes. So, I can create a list of numbers from 2 to 199 and then cross out the multiples of each prime. 

But wait, doing this manually might be time-consuming. Maybe I can list the primes in smaller chunks and then add them up as I go. Alternatively, I can use some known properties of primes to help me.
